dedupe_keys.name: ghent crowdfunding platform for urban greening and edible streets

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes crowdfunding.gent, the civic crowdfunding platform launched by the City of Ghent, Belgium, on 16 March 2015 so that citizens can propose and fund small projects, including urban greening that eases heat stress. Ghent faces rising temperatures and heatwaves, and a study cited on the page showed that more green areas reduce its urban heat island. Initiators set a funding goal, supporters give at least 10 euros, and a city platform manager checks each project against minimum conditions. Two adaptation projects were funded in 2015: Lekker Dichtbij, on urban farming, and the Edible Street, which placed planters in streets and was copied in Kortrijk, where Groene Straat realised 22 green street projects, and in Roeselare. In its first year the platform raised about 70,000 euros, 80 percent of projects met their target, and the city offers 55,000 euros a year to co-finance successful non-profit projects. The page, first published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with a link to the platform. Caveats: the platform has drifted towards socio-cultural projects, adaptation effects are not measured, and projects are small. It illustrates citizen financing of green infrastructure for climate adaptation to extreme heat; related records are the Bologna GAIA tree planting and Vrijburcht garden case studies.

outcomes: About 70,000 euros were raised in 2015 with 80 percent of projects funded, and the Edible Street idea spread to Kortrijk and Roeselare.
